questions.question: Which mathematical assertions and exact hypotheses suffice to derive the full-scope sine theorem?
questions.deliverable: Mathematical proof with step-specific source and formal witnesses, including unbounded domains.

questions.question: Which reductions are original, modern reformulations, or independent alternative proofs?
questions.deliverable: Side-by-side derivations with their different hypotheses and conclusions.

questions.question: Which historical antecedents are explicitly cited in 1970, and which are retrospective?
questions.deliverable: Page-verified historical register, not publication-date arrows.

questions.question: Where are operator domains, gap alternatives, scalar field, and ideal membership essential?
questions.deliverable: Hypothesis matrix for finite, bounded, and unbounded routes.

questions.question: How is the Section 4 extremal branch related to the main sine theorem, and why does Proposition 4.4 fail?
questions.deliverable: A mathematical branch comparison and source-specific correction.

questions.question: Which sharp estimates or eliminations are new beyond already published work?
questions.deliverable: Separate new-theorem register; prior-art and Lean proof checks before novelty claims.

hypotheses.claim: A residual/Sylvester route avoids invoking Section 4 full-displacement extremality.
hypotheses.requires: Mathematical proof review AND original-paper citation; the named Lean closure is only supporting evidence.

hypotheses.claim: Finite interval/exterior and half-infinite ordered spectral gaps require distinguishable analytic work at unbounded scope.
hypotheses.requires: Exhibit both Sylvester derivations and their form-domain assumptions.

hypotheses.claim: The modulus identification is a load-bearing bridge for the chosen positive-sine formulation.
hypotheses.requires: Check actual modulus theorem and alternative mathematical representation.

hypotheses.claim: An alternate bounded/finite proof avoids some of the full-scope mathematical prerequisites.
hypotheses.requires: State two proved routes and compare hypotheses; module counts do not qualify.
